⬇ CAD + firmware (.zip)

Plane Pointer ✈ 2-axis ADS-B tracker

An arrow on your desk that physically points at the nearest aircraft over Escondido and announces it: “Southwest one two three four, eight thousand feet, inbound Lindbergh, seven miles.” Two NEMA17s with 3:1 printed gears on TMC2209 drivers. An ESP32-S3 pulls ADS-B from adsb.lol, airplanes.live or your own RTL-SDR, and a DY-SV5W stitches the announcement from voice clips. When the sky is empty, it points at KMYF.

Key numbers from the CAD and firmware

Size
Ø160 × ~200 mm
base 85 mm tall, elevation axle 182 mm above the desk
Gearing
3 : 1 both axes
module 1.5, 16T → 48T involute spur, 48 mm centres, 0.15 mm backlash
Resolution
0.075° / µstep
200 × 8 µsteps × 3 = 4,800 steps per output rev (TMC interpolates to 256)
Slew
90°/s AZ · 60°/s EL
trapezoidal accel; 180° turn in 2.8 s (simulated in the firmware test)
Travel
∞ AZ · −5…92° EL
slip ring for continuous azimuth (or ±270° cable-wrap mode)
Homing
Hall + StallGuard
A3144 + magnet for AZ; EL drives into a printed stop at −5°, so no sensor wires go through the slip ring
Data
ADS-B every 5 s
dead-reckoned 5× per second between fetches → smooth tracking
Power
12 V · 3 A
≈ 1.2 A typical while slewing, ~0.4 A holding
Collision-checked in CAD: gear meshes show zero overlap. The elevation stop tab meets the printed stop at exactly −5°. Arrow, tail fins, elevation gear, pinion and motor were all checked against the yoke from −5° to 95°. The tail fins were narrowed to ±8 mm after the first check showed them hitting the elevation pinion at 90°.

Wiring

Notes

  • Set each TMC2209 VREF pot for about 0.8 A RMS. The firmware sets IRUN/IHOLD over UART and halves EL current while homing.
  • Both drivers share one UART line: ESP TX goes through 1 kΩ to the joined PDN_UART pins, and ESP RX connects to them directly. On a BTT v1.3, solder the PDN pad jumper.
  • The hall sensor needs ≥ 4.5 V, so power it from 5 V. Its open-collector output is safe on a 3.3 V pin with the internal pull-up.
  • No elevation sensor wires: EL homes by StallGuard (DIAG → GPIO8) against the printed stop. Only the 4 motor wires go through the slip ring.

Without a slip ring

Set SLIP_RING = False. Azimuth is then limited to ±270° and the firmware unwinds the long way around when needed. Leave a loose 4-wire loop through the Ø28 bore.

Firmware MicroPython 1.23+, ESP32-S3

FileWhat it does
main.pyasyncio app: WiFi, homing, ADS-B task, 200 ms control loop, web UI on port 80
config.pyWiFi, home lat/lon/alt, source, modes, pins, speeds, calibration
geo.pyWGS-84 ECEF→ENU az/el (curvature included), great-circle bearing, dead reckoning, “inbound/departing” guess
stepper.pytrapezoidal planner + RMT hardware step pulses in 40 ms chunks
tmc2209.pyUART register driver (stealthChop, 1/8 µstep, current, StallGuard)
dysv5w.pyDY-SV5W UART, including combination play AA 1B
announcer.pycallsign/altitude → words → clip codes; airline ICAO table
make_clips.pyrun on your PC: neural-TTS voice clips → /ZH/xx.mp3 (117 clips)
test_desktop.pyruns on a PC: checks geometry, announcements, planner

How a target becomes motion + speech

GET https://api.adsb.lol/v2/point/33.1192/-117.0864/25
  → ac[]: hex, flight, lat, lon, alt_geom, gs, track, baro_rate
every 200 ms:
  dead-reckon each aircraft (gs, track, age)
  ENU → az, el, slant range        (ignore el < 1.5°)
  pick nearest | lowest | arrivals | watch, with 15 % hysteresis
  AZ shortest path (slip ring) · EL clamp −5…92°
on new target:
  "chime Southwest one two three four
   eight thousand feet inbound Lindbergh seven miles"
  → DY-SV5W: AA 1B 1A "01""02""1N""1O"…  (one UART frame)
sky empty → point at KMYF (bearing 188°, el −0.3°)
Destination without a paid route API: a descending aircraft whose track points within 30° of a nearby airport is announced as “inbound X”; a climbing one close to an airport is “departing X”. Airline callsigns only match airline airports (Lindbergh, LAX, Ontario…). N-numbers match GA fields (Montgomery, Palomar, Gillespie…). Military fields are never guessed for airliners. Anything else falls back to “heading southwest”.
Local RTL-SDR option: run readsb/tar1090 on a Pi with any RTL-SDR dongle, then set ADSB_SOURCE = "local" and point LOCAL_URL at …/data/aircraft.json. It's the same JSON format, with no rate limits and no internet needed.

Assembly

  1. Print the parts listed above. Press heat-set inserts: 3 in the base boss top, 4 in the ring gear top.
  2. Base: fit the AZ motor under the top plate with 4× M3×8 countersunk screws, shaft up. Glue the A3144 into its pocket (flat face up) and clip the speaker into the ring under the grille.
  3. Azimuth bearing: press the 6808 onto the boss and the ring gear onto the bearing, with the magnet glued into the gear pocket first. Fit the bearing cap with 3× M3×6. The gear should spin freely and clear the plate by 1 mm.
  4. Pinion: slide the 16T pinion onto the AZ shaft, flat to the grub, top flush with the gear, then check backlash.
  5. Slip ring: drop the body into the Ø28 bore. The rotor side runs up through the gear to the yoke.
  6. Yoke: press both 625ZZ into the arms and bolt the EL motor to the outside of the +Y arm. Fit the EL pinion (hub toward the centre), then screw the yoke onto the ring gear (4× M3×10).
  7. Elevation: slide the axle through the −Y bearing, the arrow hub, the EL gear and the +Y bearing. Tighten the grubs on the axle flat with the arrow level and the gear meshed. Add M8 nuts to the tail pocket until the arrow almost balances.
  8. Electronics: build the perfboard (ESP32 + 2× TMC2209 + buck), wire it as above and close the bottom plate. Copy ZH/ to the SD card.
  9. Calibrate: after the first homing, open http://<ip>/point?az=188&el=0 and turn the whole base until the arrow points at Montgomery. Or set AZ_HOME_DEG to the true bearing the arrow faces when the hall trips.
